name: How do you know if your house can support a second-floor addition?

mainEntity.name: How do you know if your house can support a second-floor addition?
mainEntity.text: How do you know if your house can support a second-floor addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: The only reliable way to know is through a structural review by an engineer or qualified design-build team. The evaluator will look at the foundation, framing size and condition, shear strength, load paths, and any signs of settlement or cracking. Soil conditions and previous remodels also matter, because a home may have been altered in ways that affect its ability to carry extra weight. Some homes can support a second story with moderate reinforcement, while others need extensive work that changes the project budget substantially. Homeowners should not rely on general assumptions based on age or appearance. A feasibility study can save money by confirming whether upward expansion is practical before architectural plans are finalized. It can also uncover issues that affect stair placement, roof layout, and how much of the existing house must be opened up during construction.
acceptedAnswer.description: You need a structural evaluation of the foundation, framing, load paths, and soil conditions. A home that looks sound can still need major reinforcement before it can safely carry a second floor.
